item.title: Flu continues to impact local hospital
item.description: Flu continues to impact wards at Sligo University Hospital. There are currently three outbreaks in separate wards. Last week, the hospital issued a plea to those with flu-like symptoms not to visit the facility. Advertisement The three outbreaks are less than the six which were reported last week. 29 patients with flu are being treated across the hospital. item.title: Uninsured car seized in county Roscommon
item.description: A car has been seized in county Roscommon after the driver was found to be without essential documentation. Over the weekend, Gardaí stopped a car in Castlerea. The driver, who was 18-years-old was found to have no tax, insurance or NCT. Advertisement Proceedings have commenced.

item.title: Retail and bar workers continue to suffer verbal abuse
item.description: Two thirds of bar and retail workers experience verbal abuse in their workplaces. That's according to Mandate Trade Union, which is calling on employers to ensure staff are respected and fairly treated over the Christmas period. The union is also demanding safe staffing levels to prevent burnout and protect workers from health and safety risks as shops become overcrowded. item.title: Local schools to benefit from funding
item.description: Schools in the Shannonside region are set to receive nearly 45,000 euro in funding for Education for Sustainable Development projects. Minister for Education and Youth, Hildegarde Naughton has announced the delivery of over €850,000 in funding for Education for Sustainable Development projects in 390 schools across the country. item.title: Soldiers continuing Lebanon deployment
item.description: The work continues at Camp Shamrock, despite Christmas fast approaching. More than 340 Irish soldiers will spend the festive season in Lebanon, as part of a six-month UNIFIL deployment. They'll mark the occasion with a special Christmas dinner, while continuing to man their posts along 'The Blue Line' at the Israeli border. item.title: Plans Emerge for Theatre Development at Boyle Courthouse
item.description: A theatre, similar to The Dock in Carrick-on-Shannon, could be developed in Boyle Courthouse. Court sittings ended there in 2011, and the building has stood vacant ever since. The government has allocated almost 50,000 euro for a feasibility study on converting it into a theatre and community space. item.title: Greenway Set to Connect Ballinamore and Mohill
item.description: Plans will develop a greenway between Ballinamore and Mohill in Co Leitrim. It's the latest path for cyclists and walkers planned for the region. A popular greenway already links Leitrim village and Drumshanbo, and plans are underway for one between Lough Key and Carrick-on-Shannon. item.title: Charlie Doyle

item.title: Funding Secured for Roscommon’s Loughaneane Park
item.description: Roscommon's Loughaneane Park is in receipt of funding. Just over 44 and a half thousand euro will see the installation of a roof cover over the existing amphitheatre. It's hoped that, with this, it will be able to used year-round as a community and cultural space.
